name: Catedral Metropolitana de Quito
key_features: Catholic cathedral in Quito designed by military engineer Antonio García, completed 1799.

name: Casa de Nariño
key_features: Presidential palace of Colombia in Bogotá, completed 1908.

name: Bharat Mandapam
key_features: 390,000 m2 convention centre with a 7,000-seat hall and six exhibition halls; retrofuturist style.

name: Yashobhoomi (India International Convention and Expo Centre)
by: C P Kukreja Architects, IDOM and ARCOP Associates
key_features: 1 km-long foyer linking the halls, convertible auditorium seating, rainwater harvesting; IGBC Green Cities Platinum.

name: Christuskirche
key_features: Neo-Romanesque, Art Nouveau and Gothic Revival church of local quartz sandstone with Carrara marble portico.

name: Acropolium of Carthage (Cathedral of Saint Louis)
key_features: Byzantine, Gothic and Moorish styles; Latin cross plan, central cupola ringed by eight small spires.

name: Bourguiba Mausoleum
key_features: Golden dome between two green domes, flanked by two 25 m minarets at the end of a 200 m alley.

name: Abu al-Abbas al-Mursi Mosque
key_features: Neo-Mamluk exterior with a large central dome, four smaller domes and a 73 m minaret.

name: Cape Town Stadium
by: gmp Architects with Louis Karol Architects and Point Architects
key_features: Built 2007-2009 on Green Point Common for the 2010 World Cup; designed by gmp with local firms.

name: Durban City Hall
key_features: Edwardian neo-baroque city hall, almost an exact replica of Belfast City Hall; built 1906-1910.

name: Capital Museum
key_features: Stone-clad exterior wall meant to symbolise the city walls and towers of ancient China.

name: Digital Beijing Building
key_features: Solid and void alternate like 0 and 1; the ends suggest a barcode, the long faces a circuit board.

name: Presidential Office Building
key_features: A 60 m central tower, once the tallest structure in the Taipei Basin; the east front faces Ketagalan Boulevard.

name: Bug Dome
by: WEAK! (Hsieh Ying-Chun, Roan Ching-Yueh, Marco Casagrande)
key_features: Woven bamboo shell with 'weak concrete' (cement mixed with soil), inspired by the homes insects build.

name: Yuz Museum
key_features: Converted aircraft hangar at the former Longhua Airport; over 9,000 m2 with a main gallery above 3,000 m2.

name: Chengdu Museum
key_features: New city museum won in an international competition; 65,000 m2 of floor area.

name: Auditorium Building
key_features: Adler & Sullivan's 1887–89 mixed-use landmark: granite and limestone facade, 4,200-seat theatre, 17-storey tower.

name: Climatron
by: T. C. Howard (Synergetics); Murphy and Mackey
key_features: 1960 geodesic dome, 42 m across: the first fully air-conditioned greenhouse, in aluminium tubes and Plexiglas.

name: Biosphere 2
by: Space Biosphere Ventures (frame and glazing by Peter Pearce, Pearce Structures)
key_features: Space frame of steel tubing and glass over 3.14 acres, with 'lung' domes that let the air expand and contract.

name: Denver Central Library
key_features: 540,000 sq ft; abstracted classical forms, colours and materials from the past.

name: Henry J. Allen House (Allen-Lambe House)
key_features: Brick Prairie house with Ludowici tile roof and a Carthage marble water table; rooms wrap a sunken garden.

name: Dreischeibenhaus
by: Hentrich, Petschnigg & Partner (Helmut Hentrich, Hubert Petschnigg)
key_features: 'Three Plates Building': one of the first skyscrapers completed in Germany after WW2, 25 floors.

name: Detlev-Rohwedder-Haus
key_features: Seven storeys, 2,800 rooms, a reinforced-concrete skeleton faced in limestone and travertine; built 1935–36.

name: Stockholm Court House
key_features: National Romantic courthouse on Kungsholmen, built 1909–1915.

name: Military Cathedral of St. Mary Queen of Peace, Brasília
key_features: Niemeyer's triangular church in Brasília, whose form refers to a tent.

name: Stephanuskirche (Wolfsburg)
key_features: A church and parish center by Alvar Aalto, a prominent example of International modernism in Germany.

name: A. D. German Warehouse
key_features: Wright's Mayan Revival warehouse in Richland Center, the Wisconsin town where he was born.

name: National Museum of Modern Art, Tokyo
key_features: Japan's main museum of modern art, in Kitanomaru Park, known for its 20th-century collection.

name: Centro Internacional de Ferias y Congresos de Tenerife
key_features: Calatrava's 1996 trade fair and congress centre on Tenerife's seafront, with a great hall on the top floor.

name: Artigas Gardens
key_features: Gaudí's 1905–06 Modernista gardens, filled with arches and Catholic symbols, restored in 1992.

name: Malmö Opera
by: Sigurd Lewerentz, David Helldén, Erik Lallerstedt
key_features: Sigurd Lewerentz's 1933–44 Malmö theatre, now an opera house with 1,511 seats in an enclosed amphitheatre.

name: Cecil H. Green Library
key_features: Stanford's main library, with 4 million volumes, the centre of a campus library system.

name: Altes Stadthaus, Berlin
key_features: Berlin's former city hall, built 1902-11 by Ludwig Hoffmann, with five courtyards and 29 allegorical sculptures.

name: Building of the Yugoslavian legation in Berlin
key_features: Berlin's 1938-40 legation for Yugoslavia, designed by Werner March, now a listed building.

name: Leighton House
key_features: Frederic Leighton's Victorian home, with an Arab Hall of tiles bought in the Near East and Orientalist interiors.

name: Adam Mickiewicz Theatre, Cieszyn
key_features: A theatre on Theatre Square in the Old City of Cieszyn, Poland.

name: Bush House
key_features: Built 1925 to 1935 as a trade centre; by 1929 called the world's most expensive building.

name: Fresno City Hall
key_features: Arthur Erickson's post-modern, futurist city hall in Fresno, housing the mayor's office and council chambers.

name: 100 Eleventh Avenue
key_features: Jean Nouvel's 23-storey West Side tower, called 'a vision machine', with one of New York's most advanced curtain walls.

name: Frist Campus Center
key_features: Venturi's 2001 addition fills the courtyard of a Collegiate Gothic hall, now a focal point of Princeton's social life.

name: 1101 New York Avenue
key_features: A Washington office tower whose corners are notched to give more window offices.

name: Caja Mágica
key_features: A Madrid tennis centre with three courts under one structure and a series of retractable roofs.

name: 550 South Tryon
key_features: The tallest building in the world to use precast double tees, completed in 2010 in Charlotte.

name: Canadian Clay and Glass Gallery
key_features: Patkau Architects' gallery for Canadian ceramics and glass, opened in 1993 and awarded a 1997 Governor General's Medal of Excellence.

name: Bibliothèque universitaire des langues et civilisations
key_features: Paris Rive Gauche academic library, open since 2011, for all languages and civilisations beyond the Western world.

name: Huis Hillebrand
key_features: Rietveld's 1934–1935 house in The Hague, with a low tent roof that looks flat from close up.

name: Asilomar Conference Grounds
key_features: Julia Morgan's conference grounds at Pacific Grove, where she designed 16 buildings from 1913 to 1929.

name: Dům obuvi Baťa (Liberec)
key_features: A functionalist high-rise shoe store in Liberec from 1932, a cultural monument since 1987.

name: Bakkehaugen Church
key_features: A natural-concrete church in Oslo shaped like a boathouse, awarded the Betongtavlen prize for concrete.

name: Ullsteinhaus
key_features: A brick expressionist landmark in Berlin-Tempelhof, 77 m tall, and for 30 years Germany's tallest high-rise.

name: Aon Center (Los Angeles)
key_features: A slender bronze-clad modernist office tower, unusually slim for an earthquake-prone city.

name: Coliseum Theater (Seattle)
key_features: Seattle's first cinema built for movies, with elaborate terra cotta on its exterior, opened in 1916.

name: Brno Crematorium
key_features: Arnošt Wiesner's crematorium at Brno Central Cemetery, built to his plans in 1926–1929 on Jihlavská Street.

name: Shanghai Symphony Hall
key_features: Isozaki and Toyota's concert hall in Shanghai, home of the Shanghai Symphony Orchestra, opened 6 September 2014.

name: Dorfkirche Kunersdorf
key_features: A late-Expressionist brick village church in Brandenburg, listed as a monument, by Curt Steinberg.

name: B.J. Ricker House
key_features: An early Walter Burley Griffin house in Grinnell, with a roof that seems to hover over its brick block.

name: Administrative Building of Nestlé SA
key_features: Nestlé's headquarters in Vevey, designed by Jean Tschumi and built in 1959-1960.

name: Alcide De Gasperi building
key_features: Luxembourg's first skyscraper and tallest building, a 23-floor tower built in 1966 for the European Parliament's secretariat.

name: Villa Savoye
key_features: Le Corbusier's Five Points of Architecture in a single house.

name: Mill Owners' Association Building
key_features: Angled concrete fins and a ramp turn a small office into a lesson in shading.

name: Farnsworth House
key_features: A single glass room lifted above a floodplain on eight steel columns.

name: S. R. Crown Hall
key_features: A clear-span hall for architecture students, its roof hung from four exposed girders.

name: Seagram Building
key_features: Set back behind a plaza, with bronze mullions that express the frame.

name: Neue Nationalgalerie
key_features: One column-free glass hall under a steel roof resting on eight columns.

name: Johnson Wax Headquarters
key_features: A forest of slender 'lily pad' columns under a glowing glass-tube roof.

name: Rietveld Schröder House
key_features: De Stijl in three dimensions: floating planes and sliding partitions.

name: Villa Mairea
key_features: Modernism softened with timber, a forest of poles and an L-shaped courtyard.

name: Säynätsalo Town Hall
key_features: A brick town hall around a raised grass courtyard, with timber trusses over the council.

name: Glass House
key_features: A glass box whose walls are the landscape; only the bathroom is enclosed.

name: Hiroshima Peace Memorial Museum
key_features: Raised on pilotis and aligned on an axis with the A-Bomb Dome.

name: Phillips Exeter Academy Library
key_features: Books around a central atrium framed by huge circles; reading carrels at the brick edge.

name: Kimbell Art Museum
key_features: Cycloid vaults split by a slot of daylight bounced off reflectors.

name: National Assembly of Bangladesh
key_features: Geometric cut-outs carve light into a concrete citadel set in a lake.

name: Yale Art and Architecture Building
key_features: Dozens of interlocking levels and corduroy concrete: a design studio built in section.

name: Yoyogi National Gymnasium
key_features: A suspension roof hung from two concrete masts, built for the 1964 Olympics.

name: Habitat 67
key_features: 354 prefabricated modules stacked so each flat gets a garden on a neighbour's roof.

name: MASP
key_features: A 74-metre span lifts the galleries to keep the plaza and the view open.

name: SESC Pompéia
key_features: A drum factory kept as a leisure centre, with new concrete towers linked by bridges.

name: Trellick Tower
key_features: Lifts in a separate tower, bridging to the flats every third floor.

name: Sydney Opera House
key_features: Shells cut from one sphere so they could be prefabricated, on a stepped podium.

name: Gandhi Smarak Sangrahalaya
key_features: A grid of tiled pavilions around a water court, open to the breeze and able to grow.

name: Kanchanjunga Apartments
key_features: Interlocking duplexes with two-storey garden verandas instead of balconies.

name: Heritance Kandalama
key_features: A hotel laid along a rock face, so overgrown it disappears into the jungle.

name: New Gourna Village
key_features: Mud-brick vaults and domes revived to house villagers cheaply.

name: Kolumba Museum
key_features: A perforated brick veil built over the ruins of a Gothic church.

name: Row House in Sumiyoshi
key_features: A concrete box split by an open courtyard you cross to get to bed, even in the rain.

name: Sendai Mediatheque
key_features: Thirteen lattice tubes carry thin floor plates, like seaweed in a tank.

name: Teshima Art Museum
key_features: One concrete shell with two openings, cast over a mound of earth.

name: House NA
key_features: A glass house of 21 floor plates at different heights, like living in a tree.

name: Lloyd's Building
key_features: Lifts, stairs and ducts as plug-in towers around a 60-metre atrium.

name: HSBC Main Building
key_features: Floors hung from suspension trusses, freeing a public plaza beneath.

name: Guggenheim Bilbao
key_features: Titanium curves designed with CATIA, software from the aerospace industry.

name: Tate Modern
key_features: A power station turned museum; the Turbine Hall became an indoor street.

name: Jewish Museum Berlin
key_features: A zigzag plan cut through by empty 'voids' that visitors can see but not enter.

name: Oslo Opera House
key_features: A marble roof that slopes into the fjord, open for anyone to walk on.

name: Elbphilharmonie
key_features: A glass crown on a brick warehouse, with a public plaza between old and new.

name: Louvre Abu Dhabi
key_features: A 180-metre dome of layered stars casts a 'rain of light' over a museum town.

name: Metropol Parasol
key_features: Giant timber parasols over a market and Roman ruins, with a walkway on top.

name: Heydar Aliyev Center
key_features: One continuous surface folds from plaza to roof, with no line between wall and ground.

name: High Line
by: Diller Scofidio + Renfro, James Corner, Piet Oudolf
key_features: An abandoned elevated railway turned into a park in the air.
